name: AD845 (ADI 16 MHz CBFET JFET-input single, J/K/A/B/S grades)
tagline: ADI's 16 MHz, 100 V/us JFET-input CBFET single, around since at least 1990. One headphone-amp survey called it smooth and slightly valve-like while keeping ADI's punch.
technology: N-channel JFET-input monolithic op-amp built on ADI's complementary bipolar (CB) process, which is where the 'CBFET' in the datasheet title ('Precision, 16 MHz CBFET Op Amp') comes from. ADI's 12/90 Rev. A SPICE macro-model also models the input as an N-channel JFET pair.

part_numbers.status: KN: discontinued per ADI PDN 10_0081 (as reported by a search summary), replaced by KNZ; KNZ: status unconfirmed
part_numbers.notes: K grade (best commercial grade), 0 to +70 C, 8-pin PDIP. AD845KN datasheets are on alldatasheet, and a web-search summary says a PDN lists AD845KN with AD845KNZ as its replacement. SPICE worst case: Vos 0.25 mV, Ios 50 pA.

J grade in a 16-lead wide-body SOIC, NOT an 8-lead SOIC. alldatasheet has an AD845JR-16 listing (1011846). The REEL variants come only from third-party lists. Not pin-compatible with SOIC-8 sockets or adapters.
A grade, industrial -40 to +85 C (datasheet). Same worst-case Vos/Ios as J in the SPICE model. Orderable codes (e.g. AQ) were not seen.
B grade, industrial -40 to +85 C (datasheet). Same worst-case Vos/Ios as K. AD845BQ appears only in third-party lists. Q is CERDIP by ADI convention, so the package is not vendor-verified.
S grade, military -55 to +125 C (datasheet). SQ and SQ/883B appear only in third-party lists. No SMD 5962 number was seen.

lineage.period: by 12/1990 to present (Z-suffix orderables still listed by distributors); non-Z leaded versions discontinued around 2010 per PDN 10_0081 (reported)
lineage.notes: ADI SPICE macro-models dated '12/90, Rev. A' (AAG/PMI) exist for the AD845 and each grade, so a graded datasheet existed by Dec 1990. Built on ADI's complementary bipolar (CB) process. A web-search summary reports ADI PDN 10_0081 discontinuing JN/KN in favour of Pb-free JNZ/KNZ; the PDN form was not read directly. No second source was found.

reputation.summary: A niche ADI JFET single with thin enthusiast coverage. The only located listening report is a Chinese translation (DiyEden, on Soomal, 2005) of a headphone-amp op-amp survey. That one reviewer calls the AD845 smooth, with less detail than the AD843 and a slightly valve-like feel while keeping ADI's punch. It sounds looser, softer and 'slower' than Burr-Brown parts. The reviewer ranks its resolution above OPA132/134 and AD823 and below AD843/OPA627, and recommends it for mains-powered amps. A claimed 'cult following' for DAC I/V stages remains unsourced.
sonic_descriptors: resolution above OPA134/AD823, below AD843/OPA627 (one reviewer)
caveats: All listening impressions come from one reviewer's survey (via translation).
Single channel only: dual-socket rolling needs an adapter.
The SOIC version is a 16-lead wide-body package (AD845JR-16), not SOIC-8.
High quiescent current (about 10 mA, per the reviewer): poor for battery amps.
Minimum supply is +/-4.75 V (9.5 V total), which the reviewer also noted.
Fast part (100 V/us, 16 MHz): normal high-speed layout and decoupling care applies.

counterfeit_notes: No AD845-specific counterfeit reports were found. General checks: (1) ADI logo, full part number with grade letter, and a plausible date code. (2) The SOIC version is a 16-lead wide body (JR-16/JRZ-16), so an 'AD845' marked on an SOIC-8 body is suspect (inferred). (3) Supply current should be about 10 mA (reviewer figure); a relabelled low-power JFET part such as a TL071 draws far less (inferred). (4) Check for slew near 100 V/us and unity-gain bandwidth of at least 12.8 MHz (datasheet). (5) Non-Z JN/KN parts reportedly went out of production around 2010, so they should carry older date codes.

refuted_claims: The previous note that the 'CBFET' process name was unverified: the datasheet title is 'Precision, 16 MHz CBFET Op Amp', and the part is built on ADI's complementary bipolar (CB) process.
The previous note that non-Z AD845KN was not seen: AD845KN datasheet listings exist on alldatasheet, and a search summary ties AD845KN to a PDN naming AD845KNZ as its replacement.
The search-summary inference that the whole AD845 series is discontinued is not supported. Evidence shows only that non-Z JN/KN were replaced by Z parts; RS UK and Digi-Key still list the part.
corrections: Technology: confirmed CBFET, an N-JFET input on ADI's complementary bipolar process.

Datasheet: current revision is Rev. E; title and vendor PDF URL confirmed. Product page confirmed and raised to high confidence. Added 14 distributor and third-party mirrors, with older-revision candidates marked low confidence.

Grades: J/K 0 to 70 C, A/B -40 to 85 C, S -55 to 125 C (datasheet).
The reviewer's '9.5 V minimum supply' matches the datasheet +/-4.75 V minimum.
Lineage and status: added the reported PDN 10_0081 discontinuance of non-Z JN/KN (replacement JNZ/KNZ, about 2010) at medium-low confidence. Family status is still unconfirmed.
Discovery hint 'check obsolete/LTB status': partially addressed. Leaded non-Z parts were discontinued; no family-wide obsolescence notice was found.
No silicon change, die revision or fab-transfer PCN was found; silicon_changes stays empty.

revision_chain_notes: Analog Devices AD845 data sheet, the only vendor document (sole source, no second source found). Known chain, oldest to newest: (1) a graded J/K/A/B/S data sheet existed by 12/1990, inferred from the 12/90 SPICE macro-models; (2) Revs. A, B and C: letters implied, dates and copies not found; (3) Rev. D: date unknown, before 10/03; (4) Rev. E, 10/03: figures and TPCs (typical performance characteristics) renumbered, an editorial change. Rev. E is the current revision on analog.com and on radiolocman. This pass found a new Mouser copy whose title confirms Rev. E. It found no copy of the original edition or of Revs. A through D. Four searches aimed at Rev. B, C or D, early 1990s editions, databooks, datasheetarchive, farnell and the '10/03(E)' imprint returned only Rev. E or copies that do not show a revision. Still missing: the date and copies of the original edition (Rev. 0 or unlettered, circa 1989-1990), the dates and copies of Revs. A, B and C, and the date and a copy of Rev. D. The best places left to look are the older scans already listed (alldatasheet ID 48467, datasheetcatalog, octopart 65835 with the older 'a' logo, kontest.ru) and Wayback captures of the two archive seed URLs. Those seeds follow ADI's usual URL patterns for about 2004-2014 and were not confirmed for AD845 by any search result. Treat them as candidate URLs to look up in the Wayback Machine. One search summary said a docs.rs-online.com PDF holds the AD845 data sheet but did not say which of three results it meant (0900766b80ddff33, 0900766b80de075f, 0900766b80e431ff), so none was recorded. ADI Linear Products or Amplifier Reference Manual databooks from about 1990-1992 would hold the early editions, but no online copy was found in this budget.
